title: Energy and Power
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Energy and Power Worksheets (Stores, Efficiency, kWh and Costs)
standard_text: Calculation of fuel uses and costs in the domestic context: comparing energy values of different foods (from labels) (kJ); comparing power ratings of appliances in watts (W, kW); comparing amounts of energy transferred (J, kJ, kW hour); domestic fuel bills, fuel use and costs; fuels and energy resources. Energy changes and transfers: simple machines give bigger force but at the expense of smaller movement; heating and thermal equilibrium; other processes that involve energy transfer. Changes in systems: energy as a quantity that can be quantified and calculated; the total energy has the same value before and after a change.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on energy and power: energy stores, conservation, efficiency, watts and kilowatts, kilowatt-hours, the cost of electricity and energy resources. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Energy is conserved; some is always dissipated as heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is never used up; it is transferred between stores.

  • Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal. Some energy is always dissipated as heat.
  • Power is how fast energy is transferred (watts). Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h); cost = kWh × price.
  • Efficiency = useful energy ÷ total energy × 100%.
Example

2 kW heater for 3 hours?

2 × 3

Answer: 6 kWh

Example

6 kWh at 25p per kWh?

6 × 25

Answer: 150p (£1.50)

Common mistakes

  • Saying energy is used up.
  • Thinking kWh is a unit of power.
  • Thinking a device can be more than 100% efficient.

faq.q: How do you work out the cost of using an appliance?
faq.a: Multiply its power in kilowatts by the time in hours to get kilowatt-hours, then multiply by the price per kWh.
The fraction of the energy supplied that is transferred usefully: useful energy ÷ total energy × 100%.

faq.q: What is the difference between power and energy?
faq.a: Energy is measured in joules or kilowatt-hours. Power is how fast energy is transferred, measured in watts.

items.q: Zara's ball keeps 60% of its height on each bounce. Dropped from 80 cm, it reaches 48 cm on the first bounce. About how high is the second bounce?
Poppy's ball keeps 50% of its height on each bounce. Dropped from 200 cm, it reaches 100 cm on the first bounce. About how high is the second bounce?
Ethan observes: “A cyclist pedals harder and speeds up.” Where does the energy come from or go?
c: To the glove and hand as thermal energy and sound
items.e: Energy is never used up; it moves from one place to another.

items.e: Energy is never used up; it moves from one place to another.

items.q: Evie's ball keeps 50% of its height on each bounce. Dropped from 80 cm, it reaches 40 cm on the first bounce. About how high is the second bounce?
Which energy store is mainly filled in a moving car?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: Can energy be created or destroyed?
c: No. It can only be transferred from one store to another.

items.q: What does dissipated energy mean?
c: energy that spreads out to the surroundings, usually as heat, and is not useful

items.q: Leo observes: “A hockey stick hits a puck.” Which statement about the object's kinetic energy is correct?
c: Kinetic energy is transferred to the puck.
Kinetic energy is transferred from the puck.
items.e: When an object speeds up, energy goes into it; when it slows down, energy leaves it.

items.q: Ruby drops a ball from 200 cm. It bounces back to only 150 cm. What best explains this?

Gravity turned off at the top.
